title: Traders do not believe this rally: Credit Suisse's Mandy Xu
description: Mandy Xu, Credit Suisse, on whether traders believe this rally. With CNBC's Brian Sullivan and the Fast Money traders, Tim Seymour, Karen Finerman, Steve Grasso and Guy Adami. asr.full_text: Let's bring in a special guest, Mandy Zhu of Credit Suisse, Chief Derivatives Strategist there. Mandy, it's a pleasure to have you on Fast Money again, although I can't wait till everybody's back around the table with Melissa and the gang. So Mandy, I'll start with you. How relevant is, quote, earning season going to be, if I mean super important or not important at all, given what's going on? Thanks, Ryan. Yeah, that's a great question. I would say what has the price is in the market. Coming round of earnings will be less important than normal. So what to keep in mind is that the upcoming first quarter earnings is mostly going to cover a period before we enter a lockdown. So the informational value going forward it's not going to be a lot lot right. So I think that's important to keep in mind. And so what are you watching then in your team Mandy most closely? Sure I think what is really interesting in the derivatives market right now is you know with this bounce off of the low market up you know 20 plus percent we're not seeing any upside chasing in the market. In fact investors have been using this rally to access down side hedges. They're buying downside puts in the major indices like S&P, Russell 2000 etcetera. Which to me is actually very notable because typically in these major market corrections we do see a fair amount of upside call buying as people come in to pick the bottom, that activity, that flow is completely absent. So to me, it signals a very high amount of skepticism that this rally can continue going forward. Okay. Yeah. And I mean, what is the biggest, there's so many risks, Mandy, I feel silly even asking this question. What's the biggest risk right now? And we're talking, of course, we're talking about equity markets, what's the biggest risk right now? And of course, we're talking about equity markets, what we do here on CNBC. Sure. I think what people are watching for, the near-term data, everyone I think by this point recognizes is going to be absolutely horrific, whether you're talking about unemployment, GDP, earnings, etc. I think what will really drive market. If you're looking toward the next next leg higher. We really need to see constructive data coming from either the underlying virus in terms of a peak in the infection rates or signs that we can get the economy back to normal faster than expected. So I think that's what everyone is watching. Not so much the near term data, because that's been, I would say, completely written off. But more signs of the second half. What type of rebound? What kind of recovery are we going to get? Is it that V-shaped recovery or, you know, with some, you know, if you look at a lot of Asian economies going to lockdown, you know, I'm having more conversations with clients talking about, you know, a second wave ofK OF INSPECTION AND A POTENTIAL W- SHAPE OR W-SHAPE RECOVERY W. I THINK THAT IS WHAT MOST INVESTORS ARE FOCUSING ON AT THIS POINT. MANDY IS YOUR CREDIT SUITE. THEY LOOK FORWARD TO SEEING YOU ON THE SET SOON. THANK YOU VERY MUCH.
